chunks: We were told by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: We were told by my father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from more than one, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), that he said:

The one who wakes up at the morning, finding the coolness of our love upon his heart, let him praise Allah for the initiator of graces. It was said: And what is the initiator of graces? He said: Having a good birth.

key_terms.بَادِئُ النِّعَمِ: initiator of graces (the first or primary blessing)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir mean by the 'initiator of graces' (badi' al-ni'm) in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies 'good birth' (Tayyib al-Mawlud) as the primordial grace (Badi' al-Ni'ma), linking physical lineage to spiritual comfort. This concept underscores the Shia belief that the purity of the Prophet's household serves as the foundational vessel for divine guidance, making gratitude for one's origin a precursor to deeper theological understanding.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdullah, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by my father, from his grandfather, Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammed bin Isa, from ‘Ubaid, from Abu Muhammed al-Ansari, from more than one, from Abu Ja’far al-Baqir, peace be upon them both [1], that he said:

The one who wakes up at the morning, finding the coolness of our love upon his heart, let him praise Allah for the initiator of graces. It was said: And what is the initiator of graces? He said: Having a good birth.
